label: Late-episode D1 after a rewarded S1 visit, strongest after rare a2->S1, growing with trial.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 70, 0) ;; (in_rew == 1) * (prev_state == 1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0) ;; (phase == D1) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0)
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 60, 0) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (in_rew == 0) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 80, 0)
explanation: Fires only at D1 and only late in the episode (from ~trial 70-80, ramping up to trial 99). Its magnitude is set by the previous trial: largest after a rare a2->S1 rewarded trial (ramp starting ~trial 70), moderate after a rewarded S1 visit in general (a1 S1 r), and near zero after unrewarded trials or S2 visits, where the late-episode timing baseline is cancelled (negative late-D1 ramp term). Belief, the trial before, and the current choice add little (profile reference scores ~0). The free fit just splits the ramps more finely (separate a1 S1 r, unrewarded and S2 ramps) and adds only ~0.02 dev R^2 over the short form.

issues: Minor: the worst-fit windows are mostly the first cell of a window (previous trial '?'). There the feature fires at about 3 but the prediction is about 0.05, because the previous trial falls outside the window. This is a data limitation, not a systematic model error, and the mean error for D1 after '?' is only +0.022.

The third term, a negative late-D1 ramp, is partly a fitted correction: it cancels the per-decile timing baseline so that non-S1-rewarded D1 steps come out near zero. Dropping it lowers test R^2 from 0.79 to 0.68. Its meaning ('near zero otherwise') is real, but the label does not state it outright.

The checks support every claim. The feature is D1-only: the GO and D2 baselines and residuals are all 0. Splitting a1 S1 r and a2 S1 r into separate ramps gives test R^2 0.778, about the same as the recorded 0.786. Swapping the rewarded-S1 term for any reward at all drops it to 0.62. Using belief_lo in its place gives 0.65. Using rare transition (prev_common == 0) in place of a2 S1 r gives 0.61. Without the a2 S1 r term (S1-rewarded ramps only) it falls to 0.58. A plain linear ep_trial in place of the ramps gives 0.39. The ramp onsets are robust: 60, 70 and 75 give 0.78 to 0.786, and moving the other two onsets to 85 gives 0.786.
Systematic errors in misses are small (|mean error| <= 0.013 by phase x previous trial), so no large error class remains.
